plan.change:
Make the task harder by BREADTH, not by one more visible bug. Opus solved the current
version by reading the code and patching a few readable defects in 4-35 commands, 4-5 times out of 5
(adding a third or fourth readable bug changed nothing). Rework it so that a correct solution must
satisfy at least 8 INDEPENDENT requirements, each a different class of edge case that:
- appears only on verify-time inputs the solver never sees (the tests generate fresh inputs),
- is not visible by reading one file: it comes from how the data and the components behave
  (empty, duplicate or out-of-order records, boundary values, unit or encoding quirks, ordering of
  operations, idempotency, partial failures, large inputs),
- is stated in the instruction as one short observable rule (fairness: nothing the tests check may
  be unstated, and no rule may be a description of the defect),
- is checked by its own test(s) on at least 3 fresh inputs.
The environment must contain realistic data and code where those cases genuinely occur. A solution
that handles the obvious cases but misses any one of the 8 rules must fail. Keep the tests
deterministic, keep the instruction outcome-only and short per rule, and keep the oracle passing 3/3.

gate_problems: behavior_in_task_description: The instruction requires documented event rules, schemas, aggregates, constraints, and indicator behavior, but the available README only specifies basic fields, revision handling, weights, and severity; many required details are not explicitly documented.

behavior_in_tests: The tests cover several core cases, but do not verify all stated requirements such as complete manifest/chunk ordering invariance, exact rejected aggregates, zero-count groups, all schema constraints and indexes, or the full indicator rule set.
anti_cheating_measures: The runtime source includes repaired_importer.py alongside importer_bad.py, exposing a likely repaired implementation that can be copied rather than independently derived.

hardcoded_solution: The supplied solution can use the repaired_importer.py file placed in the environment, which is a direct ground-truth shortcut rather than demonstrating an independently derived repair process.

valid_failure_modes: The task depends on event rules and an exact schema that are not fully specified in the instruction or README, so a capable implementation can fail due to ambiguity rather than engineering difficulty.
structured_data_schema: The instruction does not document the exact SQLite table schemas, columns, types, keys, foreign keys, indexes, metadata entries, or aggregate semantics required by the tests.

oracle_investigates: The solution has a repaired_importer.py artifact available in the environment, so it can rely on author-provided ground truth instead of deriving the repair from the task and observable state.
